newsitem.title: UKRAINE: Estonian Air keeps Kiev route open after tax row.
newsitem.headline: Estonian Air keeps Kiev route open after tax row.

text.p: Estonian Air will continue flying from Tallinn to Kiev as it has solved a row with Kiev aviation authorities over a 15 percent tax on ticket sales, the Baltic state flag-carrier said on Thursday.
Leonid Lytvyns Ukraine had dropped the tax which has been imposed on foreign firms on routes not served by Ukrainian carriers.
"The problem was very serious. The Ukrainian side insisted on a 15 percent tax. But the row has been solved recently," Lytvynenko said.
"We will not pay it. It's up to the Ukrainians why they do not fly to Tallinn. No one is stopping Ukraine from flying to Estonia," he added.
Finnair and Scandinavian Airlines (SAS) both stopped flights to Kiev in 1995 after Ukraine imposed the 15 percent tax on ticket sales.
"So far we have no plans to resume the Helsinki-Kiev route because the tax problem has not been resolved," Dmytro Zinchenko, Finnair's commercial director in Kiev, told Reuters.
"We'll wait until Ukraine joins the International Civil Aviation Organisation and other international bodies. They will be forced to change conditions and cancel the tax."
He said Finnair would restart its three flights a week if Kiev lifted the tax.
SAS has closed its Kiev office and officials were not available for comment.
State carrier Air Ukraine does not fly to any Scandinavian country and passengers have to use Estonian Air, which flies three times a week to Kiev, Latvian Baltic Air or Lufthansa to get to Ukraine.
